Chapter 11: Gratitude and the Joy of Small Things.
When you picture life as an astronaut, it’s easy to get caught up in the big, dramatic moments—rockets blasting off, landings, major milestones. But you know what? For a lot of astronauts, the true magic isn’t just in those headline moments. It’s in the little things: a quick laugh with a crewmate, a familiar meal, or just quietly soaking in the sunrise as it curves over the edge of Earth.
There’s this story I love about a crew member, thousands of miles from home, finding comfort in something simple—a well-brewed cup of coffee. Picture that: the taste, the warmth, the routine of it. It’s more than just a drink. For them, it’s a touchstone—a daily reminder of home and a small pleasure that cuts through the stress and the strangeness.
Another astronaut talks about floating weightless, slowly spinning, just… marveling at how truly bizarre and wonderful it all is. Moments like these remind them—and us—that happiness can be found in the quiet details.
Most of us spend our lives chasing the next big thing—a promotion, an adventure, a goal. But if you ask someone who’s lived among the stars, they’ll tell you: the real joy is right here, in the present moment, in the tiny details and the genuine connections we make.
Gratitude becomes a real, everyday practice for astronauts. Think about it—the chance to work with a passionate team, to learn something new, to literally see the world from a whole new angle. These aren’t just perks; they’re genuine gifts. And the folks who seem happiest up there? They’re the ones who notice those gifts, who find reasons to be grateful—even on the tough days.
But here’s the thing: you don’t need to go to space to learn this lesson. Anyone—no matter where you are—can find meaning in a kind word, a shared dinner, or a peaceful walk outside. Gratitude isn’t about pretending everything’s perfect. It’s about seeing what’s good, even when life gets messy, and letting those small joys carry you through.
